unit.title: Change of State: The Translative Case

stories.summary: Carlos and his friend Zoltán renovate an old storage room into a cozy community workshop and café space.

stories.title: Önkéntesként a táborban
stories.summary: Carlos and Eszter spend a week as volunteers organizing activities at a youth summer camp near the Danube Bend.

stories.title: Névnap a nagymamánál
stories.summary: Carlos attends a traditional Hungarian Name Day celebration for Eszter's grandmother, learning visiting etiquette, toasting, and respectful deferential language.

stories.title: Az út, amit sosem felejtek el
stories.summary: A first-person account of a hiking trip in the Bakony hills that turns into an unexpected storm, a shelter, and a story worth remembering.

stories.title: Élmények, amik megváltoztattak
stories.summary: A first-person reflection on the experiences of the last ten years — a first solo trip abroad, learning to cook from a grandmother, and looking back at how much the narrator has changed.

stories.title: János vitéz útja
stories.summary: An adapted retelling of the opening of Petőfi's folk epic János vitéz: an orphaned goose-herd loses his geese, is driven from home, says goodbye to the girl he loves, and sets out to become a soldier.
stories.author: Sándor Petőfi

stories.title: Hét krajcár
stories.summary: An adapted retelling of Zsigmond Móricz's short story: an adult narrator remembers a poor but warm childhood afternoon spent with his mother, searching the house for seven missing krajcárs.
stories.author: Zsigmond Móricz

stories.title: Az arany ember
stories.summary: An adapted retelling of Mór Jókai's novel Az arany ember: a poor young riverboat worker, Tímár Mihály, rises to become a wealthy, respected merchant through careful planning, hard work and perseverance.
stories.author: Mór Jókai

stories.title: Bede Anna tartozása
stories.summary: An adapted retelling of Kálmán Mikszáth's short story: a grieving widow receives a bureaucratic demand to pay her late daughter's small old debt, and the village notary must decide how to advise and help her.
stories.author: Kálmán Mikszáth

stories.title: Nyilas Misi és a barátság próbája
stories.summary: An adapted retelling inspired by Zsigmond Móricz's novel Légy jó mindhalálig: a poor scholarship boy at the Debrecen boarding school is entrusted with money that goes missing, and must rebuild the trust of his closest friend and classmates despite the injustice.
stories.author: Zsigmond Móricz

stories.title: Kopjáss István és az új állás
stories.summary: An adapted retelling inspired by Zsigmond Móricz's classic novel Rokonok: Kopjáss István unexpectedly wins election to a prestigious town leadership post, confronting sudden career elevation, new responsibilities, and a swarm of relatives seeking office favours.
stories.author: Zsigmond Móricz

stories.title: A rossz tanuló felel
stories.summary: An adapted retelling inspired by Frigyes Karinthy's humorous masterpiece Tanár úr kérem: an unprepared student is called up to the blackboard, experiencing the universal drama of school oral examination and attempting to bluff his way through.
stories.author: Frigyes Karinthy

stories.title: A glogovai utazás
stories.summary: An adapted retelling inspired by Kálmán Mikszáth's beloved classic novel Szent Péter esernyője: travelers journey by carriage through the rugged northern mountains and muddy roads toward Glogova, pursuing the mysterious umbrella said to hold miraculous fortunes.
stories.author: Kálmán Mikszáth

stories.title: Esti Kornél és az orvosi vizsgálat
stories.summary: An adapted retelling inspired by Dezső Kosztolányi's witty literary masterpiece Esti Kornél: Esti visits an elderly, experienced professor for a medical checkup, reflecting on human vulnerability, the art of reassurance, and the profound connection between bodily health and peace of mind.
stories.author: Dezső Kosztolányi

stories.title: Édes Anna a Krisztinavárosban
stories.summary: In this adapted excerpt from Dezső Kosztolányi's masterpiece Édes Anna, Mrs. Vizy meticulously inspects the spotless bourgeois flat in Krisztinaváros before the quiet country girl Anna steps across the threshold into her new home.

stories.title: Nyilas Misi Debrecen városában
stories.summary: In this adapted literary excerpt from Zsigmond Móricz's beloved classic Légy jó mindhalálig, young student Misi navigates the historic streets and proud civic community of Debrecen, learning responsibility as he visits the blind old gentleman Mr. Pósalaky.

stories.title: Szindbád és a vasárnapi ebéd
stories.summary: In this adapted excerpt from Gyula Krúdy's world-famous Szindbád stories, the nostalgic traveler Szindbád savors the sacred ritual of Sunday lunch in a quiet old-world tavern, contemplating the steaming golden broth, marrow bones, and freshly grated horseradish.

stories.title: A vörösingesek követe és a kiáltvány a grundon
stories.summary: An adaptation from Ferenc Molnár's immortal classic novel 'A Pál utcai fiúk'. On the Paul Street playground, Boka and his friends receive startling news: the rival Redshirts intend to conquer their lot. Boka drafts an official proclamation and posts it for everyone to read.
stories.author: Molnár Ferenc

stories.title: A delejes gépember és a jövő masinái
stories.location: Budapest, New York kávéház és műhely
stories.summary: An adaptation inspired by the visionary satirical writings of Frigyes Karinthy on technology, thinking machines, and communication. Karinthy visits an eccentric inventor's workshop in Budapest, where a thinking metal machine attempts to write poetry.
stories.author: Karinthy Frigyes
stories.work: Így írtok ti / Tanár úr kérem és egyéb tárcák

stories.title: A bécsi színházban és a bál forgatagában
stories.summary: An adaptation from Mór Jókai's masterwork 'A kőszívű ember fiai' (The Baron's Sons). In glamorous imperial Vienna, young Ödön and Richard Baradlay attend the opera and the grand charity ball, experiencing the heights of high society, theater, music, and the gathering storm of Hungarian patriotism.
stories.author: Jókai Mór

stories.title: A lámpás és az erdő csendje
stories.summary: An adaptation from Géza Gárdonyi's celebrated writings on Hungarian village nature and forests. The village teacher walks through the ancient Bakony forest at twilight, reflecting on the beauty of nature, the harmony of living creatures, and mankind's sacred duty to protect the woods.
stories.author: Gárdonyi Géza

stories.title: A fillér értéke és az emberség
stories.summary: An adaptation from Zsigmond Móricz's heart-rending stories of social realism ('Hét krajcár'). In a small, modest home, a mother and her young son search every corner for seven lost pennies to buy soap to wash clothes, turning hardship into a moment of pure laughter, solidarity, and indestructible human dignity.
stories.author: Móricz Zsigmond

stories.title: A képviselő úr választási beszéde
stories.summary: An adaptation from Kálmán Mikszáth's satirical masterpieces on Hungarian parliamentary politics and election campaigns ('A képviselő úr'). In a small county town, the aspiring MP delivers a grand, flowery speech promising golden bridges and prosperity, while the sensible townspeople listen with wry humor and shrewd common sense.
stories.author: Mikszáth Kálmán

stories.title: A gavallérok és a bankhitel
stories.summary: An adaptation inspired by Kálmán Mikszáth's sharp satirical masterpiece 'A gavallérok' (The Cavaliers). In the 19th-century Hungarian countryside, aristocratic gentlemen who live beyond their means gather at the county fair, attempting to negotiate loans and keep up the appearance of wealth with wit, charm, and empty pockets.
stories.author: Mikszáth Kálmán

stories.title: Magyarázom a bizonyítványomat
stories.summary: An adaptation of Frigyes Karinthy's immortal comic masterpiece 'Magyarázom a bizonyítványomat' from 'Tanár úr kérem'. Walking home with an unfortunate report card, the student rehearses an elaborate, philosophical defense for his father, weaving past conditionals and hypothetical excuses to solve an impossible problem.
stories.author: Karinthy Frigyes

stories.title: A rossz tanuló felel
stories.summary: An adaptation of Frigyes Karinthy's classic 'A rossz tanuló felel' from 'Tanár úr kérem'. Called to the blackboard unprepared, student Ábrahám deploys every rhetorical weapon: dramatic pauses, evidential hints ('állítólag', 'biztosan'), clearing his throat, and attempting to construct an argument out of thin air while the teacher watches with ironic patience.
stories.author: Karinthy Frigyes

stories.title: A jövő század regénye
characters: Tatrangi Dávid, a zseniális magyar feltaláló
Kins- gating és a nemzetközi tudósok
stories.location: A Duna-parti kísérleti műhely és az égbolt
stories.summary: An adaptation of Mór Jókai's visionary science-fiction work 'A jövő század regénye' (1872). The brilliant Hungarian inventor Dávid Tatrangi develops the 'Aerodrom'—an electrically-powered flying machine made of an indestructible lightweight alloy ('ichor'). Looking ahead into the future, the characters discuss the breathtaking possibilities, the technological risks, and whether visionary predictions can truly alter the fate of humanity.
stories.author: Jókai Mór

stories.title: A fekete város
characters: Németh úr, a városi tanács esküdtje
stories.location: A lőcsei városháza tanácsterme és a piactér
stories.summary: An adaptation of Kálmán Mikszáth's masterwork 'A fekete város'. In the historic Zipser town of Lőcse, Judge Fabriczy and the town council face a fateful dilemma after the killing of the county deputy lieutenant: should they adhere strictly to the unbending letter of municipal law, or seek a peaceful political compromise before hatred engulfs both city and county?
stories.author: Mikszáth Kálmán

stories.title: Iskola a határon
characters: Bébé (Both Benedek), a növendék és elbeszélő
Bognár tiszthelyettes, az iskola vasfegyelmének őre
stories.location: A kőszegi katonai alreáliskola udvara és hálóterme
stories.summary: An adaptation of Géza Ottlik's philosophical classic 'Iskola a határon' (School at the Frontier). Arriving at the rigorous military boarding school in Kőszeg, the cadets Bébé, Medve, and Szulovszky discover that the institution functions like a colossal, impassive mechanism. They gradually learn how every component of the school apparatus operates, how to adapt without losing their souls, and how genuine human solidarity survives inside the most unbending clockwork.
stories.author: Ottlik Géza

stories.title: Légy jó mindhalálig
characters: A Debreceni Református Kollégium tanári kara
stories.location: A Debreceni Református Kollégium oratóriuma és az udvar
stories.summary: An adaptation of Zsigmond Móricz's tender and profound classic 'Légy jó mindhalálig' (Be Faithful Unto Death). In the historic Reformed Collegium of Debrecen, the young student Nyilas Misi undergoes a heartbreaking and transformative maturation. Unjustly accused of stealing a lottery ticket, Misi endures humiliation, but emerges from the trial with an ironclad resolve: to remain pure, honest, and dedicated to educating humanity.
stories.author: Móricz Zsigmond

stories.title: Édes Anna
characters: Édes Anna, a tiszta lelkű cselédlány
stories.summary: An adaptation of Dezső Kosztolányi's masterpiece 'Édes Anna' (1926). Set in Budapest in the autumn of 1919, Anna arrives as a maid at the bourgeois Vizy household. Untiring, silent, and obedient, she works day and night without boundaries, keeping the apartment spotless. Yet while Mrs. Vizy boasts of her 'perfect machine', Anna's soul is crushed by the total absence of human warmth, rest, and personal balance—a haunting warning against treating human beings merely as working tools.
stories.author: Kosztolányi Dezső

stories.title: A Pál utcai fiúk
characters: Nemecsek Ernő, a Pál utcaiak egyetlen közlegénye
Boka János, a Pál utcaiak igazságos és érett elnöke
Áts Feri, a vörösingesek nemes lelkű vezére
stories.location: Budapest, a Pál utcai grund és a Füvészkert
stories.summary: An adaptation of Ferenc Molnár's universally celebrated masterpiece 'A Pál utcai fiúk' (The Paul Street Boys). Set in 1889 Budapest, the boys of Pál Street defend their sacred playground—the Grund—against the rival Redshirts led by Feri Áts. The quiet, fragile private Nemecsek Ernő proves that true greatness, honor, and loyalty do not belong to ranks or physical stature, giving his very life to defend his friends and the soil of freedom.
stories.author: Molnár Ferenc

stories.title: Szent Péter esernyője
characters: Bélyi János, a glogovai szegény pap
stories.summary: An adaptation of Kálmán Mikszáth's warm, ironical, and delightful masterpiece 'Szent Péter esernyője' (St. Peter's Umbrella). In the impoverished Upper Hungarian hamlet of Glogova, a ragged red umbrella mysteriously left over an orphan baby girl during a rainstorm is heralded by superstitious peasants as a miracle from Saint Peter. Years later, brilliant young lawyer György Wibra searches the region for the umbrella, believing his eccentric late father hid a fortune in negotiable bonds in its hollow handle. But upon discovering Veronka, Wibra realizes that love and integrity far eclipse lost bank notes.
stories.author: Mikszáth Kálmán

stories.title: Egy polgár vallomásai
stories.location: Kassa, a Fő utca és Nyugat-Európa nagyvárosai
stories.summary: An adaptation of Sándor Márai's immortal autobiographical classic 'Egy polgár vallomásai' (Confessions of a Bourgeois). Raised in the patrician harmony of historic Kassa (Košice), young Márai absorbs the stern European bourgeois virtues: intellectual honesty, civic duty, and devotion to culture. Leaving his native town to wander across Weimar Germany and Paris, he experiences the dislocation of exile, yet discovers that no matter how far he travels, his true, indestructible homeland is the Hungarian language.
stories.author: Márai Sándor

stories.title: Abigél
characters: Vitay Gina, elkényeztetett, majd megedződött diáklány
Kőnig tanár úr, a Matula szelíd latin tanára (a titkos Abigél)
stories.location: Árkod, a Matula leánynevelő intézet és a park
stories.summary: An adaptation of Magda Szabó's universally beloved masterpiece 'Abigél' (Abigail). Set in 1943-44, the pampered Budapest general's daughter Gina Vitay is abruptly hidden in the strict Calvinist girls' boarding school 'Matula' in the eastern fortress town of Árkod. Rebellious at first, Gina slowly discovers that behind the school's austere discipline lies profound humanity. When mortal danger closes in, Gina discovers that the legendary miracle-working statue 'Abigél'—who secretly assists desperate girls—is actually the gentle, mocked Latin teacher Kőnig, an unheralded hero saving innocent lives from the horrors of war.
stories.author: Szabó Magda

stories.title: Az ember tragédiája
characters: Ádám, az első ember és az emberiség szellemi vándora
Éva, az élet, a szerelem és a megújulás jelképe
Lucifer, a tagadás és a rideg értelem szelleme
Az Úr, a teremtő és a remény forrása
stories.location: A Földön kívüli űr és a jövőbeli társadalom színterei
stories.summary: An adaptation of Imre Madách's philosophical dramatic poem 'Az ember tragédiája' (The Tragedy of Man, 1861), one of the supreme achievements of Hungarian literature. Adam, guided by Lucifer, travels through human history and peers into the future of society—from ancient civilizations, revolutions, and London capitalism to a sterile futuristic Phalanstery and an icy, dying Earth. Confronted with the terrifying risks of scientific coldness and loss of spirit, Adam is saved by Eve's maternal love and the Lord's transcendent command to perpetually strive and believe: 'Mondottam, ember: küzdj és bízva bízzál!'
stories.author: Madách Imre

stories.title: Az arany ember
characters: Timár Mihály, a tehetséges hajóbiztos, később gazdag kereskedő ('az arany ember')
Tímea, a török pasa leánya, Timár hűséges, de hűvös felesége
Noémi, a Senki szigetén élő tiszta lelkű leány
Teréza mama, Noémi édesanyja, a sziget békéjének őrzője
stories.location: A Duna, Komárom, a Balaton és a Senki szigete
stories.summary: An adaptation of Mór Jókai's immortal romantic masterpiece 'Az arany ember' (The Man with the Golden Touch / The Man of Gold, 1872). Timár Mihály, a humble cargo-ship captain on the Danube, miraculously saves the daughter of a fleeing Turkish pasha and stumbles upon a sunken fortune. Everything he touches turns to gold; he becomes a wealthy merchant, an honored councillor, and marries the cold, grateful Tímea. Yet wealth brings him agonizing guilt and emptiness. Only on the idyllic, untouched 'Senki szigete' (Nobody's Island), in the tender love of Noémi, does Timár find true redemption, ultimately leaving his fortune behind to live in peace and harmony with nature.
stories.author: Jókai Mór

stories.title: Szent Péter esernyője
characters: Bélyi János, a glogovai fiatal, jámbor katolikus pap
Veronka, a pap húga, akit a csodás esernyő védett meg
Wibra Gyuri, tehetséges fiatal ügyvéd Besztercebányáról
Gregorics Pál, Gyuri különc, gazdag édesapja
Adameczné és a glogovai hívek, akik Szent Péter csodájában hisznek
stories.location: Glogova, Besztercebánya és a felvidéki hegyek
stories.summary: An adaptation of Mikszáth Kálmán's humorous and touching classic 'Szent Péter esernyője' (Saint Peter's Umbrella, 1895). In the impoverished mountain village of Glogova, a young priest finds an abandoned baby girl—his orphaned sister Veronka. During a sudden storm, a miraculous worn red umbrella is placed over her basket, giving rise to local legends that Saint Peter himself brought it. As Glogova prospers and Veronka grows up, young lawyer Gyuri Wibra discovers his late eccentric father hid a lost fortune inside the umbrella's handle. Traveling to find it, Gyuri falls in love with Veronka and realizes genuine love far surpasses all worldly riches.
stories.author: Mikszáth Kálmán

stories.title: A gólyakalifa
stories.summary: An adaptation from Mihály Babits's brilliant psychological novel 'A gólyakalifa' (The Caliph Stork). Elemér Tábory, an aristocratic young intellectual, wrestles with the dual nature of reality and consciousness: in his waking hours he lives in luxury and refinement, yet each night he dreams of living as a tormented, destitute apprentice. Weighed down by opposing truths, he seeks to understand whether our identity is a single path or a complex balance of conflicting realities.
stories.author: Babits Mihály

stories.title: Utas és holdvilág
stories.summary: An adaptation from Antal Szerb's masterpiece 'Utas és holdvilág' (Journey by Moonlight). Mihály, wandering alone through the ancient stone alleys of an Italian hill town beneath the moonlight, is overwhelmed by the memories of his youth in Budapest with Tamás and Éva Ulpius. He reflects on all the paths not taken: what would have happened if he had lived differently, if he had never conformed to bourgeois adulthood, and if the past could ever truly be recovered.
stories.author: Szerb Antal

stories.title: Egri csillagok: A várvédők esküje
stories.summary: An adaptation from Géza Gárdonyi's celebrated national epic 'Egri csillagok' (Stars of Eger). In 1552, Captain István Dobó gathers his small garrison of Hungarian defenders inside the battered stone walls of Eger Castle against the overwhelming Ottoman sultanic army. Dobó delivers his legendary oath: 'A falak ereje nem a kőben van, hanem a védők lelkében' (The strength of the walls is not in the stone, but in the soul of the defenders), inspiring his men and women to triumph through unity, determination, and independent spirit.
stories.author: Gárdonyi Géza

stories.title: Pacsirta elutazik: Csend és kimondatlan szavak
stories.summary: Vajkay Ákos and his wife Antónia see their beloved, unmarried daughter Pacsirta off at the provincial railway station in Sárszeg. Once the train departs, a strange, unspoken relief begins to surface beneath their grief.
stories.author: Kosztolányi Dezső

stories.title: Utazás a régi Pest-Budán a vörös postakocsival
stories.summary: Rezeda Kázmér and Szindbád wander through the autumn mist of old Pest-Buda, where the crimson stagecoach, candlelit coffeehouse windows, and forgotten melodies evoke a vanished world of youth and memory.
stories.author: Krúdy Gyula

stories.title: A stílusparódia művészete: Így írtok ti
stories.summary: In the bustling New York Coffeehouse of 1912 Budapest, Frigyes Karinthy unveils Így írtok ti—a work that goes beyond mere wordplay to dissect the stylistic mannerisms, favorite word-formation patterns, and hidden psychology of Hungary's greatest writers.
stories.author: Karinthy Frigyes

stories.title: Bánk bán és Tiborc panasza
stories.summary: In the darkened halls of the royal palace, the nobleman Bánk bán listens to the old peasant Tiborc pour out the suffering of the common people under corrupt foreign courtiers, struggling between his oath to the king and his duty to his homeland.
stories.author: Katona József

stories.title: Ábel a Hargita fenyveseiben
stories.summary: High in the snow-covered pine forests of the Hargita mountains, young Ábel learns from his father how to live in harmony with nature, solitude, and ancestral Székely wisdom while tending the forest timber depot.
stories.author: Tamási Áron

stories.title: A festő látomása és a varázsló kertje
stories.summary: A young painter obsessed with capturing unseen harmonies of light wanders into a mysterious walled garden at dusk, where an old master teaches him how outer forms dissolve into inner vision.
stories.author: Csáth Géza
stories.work: A varázsló kertje és más novellák (1908)

stories.title: Utazás a koponyám körül: A megfigyelő elme
stories.summary: When Frigyes Karinthy begins hearing phantom trains in a Budapest coffeehouse, he turns his own neurological crisis into a rigorous scientific investigation, observing every symptom and surgical step with unwavering analytical clarity.
stories.author: Karinthy Frigyes

stories.title: Lelkiismeret, kötelesség és gyógyítás
stories.summary: As Kárász Nelli tends to her gravely ill husband and speaks with the village physician, both confront the haunting questions of medical ethics and personal conscience: what could have been prevented, and where duty ends and guilt begins.
stories.author: Németh László

stories.title: Az abszurd logikája: Egyperces történetek
stories.summary: At a provincial tram stop and an information window, an ordinary passenger and a calm clerk explore a world where official instructions follow impeccable formal logic—yet lead to complete absurdity.
stories.author: Örkény István

stories.title: Tanárok, könyvek és eszmélkedés
stories.summary: In a turn-of-the-century provincial gymnasium, the young student Imre Sátordy discovers the rigors and quiet exhilaration of intellectual awakening as his classical literature teacher makes him translate Latin poets and defend his own aesthetic judgments.
stories.author: Babits Mihály

stories.title: Störr kapitány kételyei és az önvizsgálat
stories.summary: Haunted by contradictory impressions and restless dreams in a foggy port city, the Dutch sea captain Jakob Störr reflects on his marriage to the elusive Frenchwoman Lizzy, discovering that jealousy and self-deception reveal as much about his own unconscious as about his wife.
stories.author: Füst Milán

stories.title: Berend Iván kísérletei és a bányamérnök találmánya
stories.summary: In the coal mines of Bondavölgy, the scientist-engineer Iván Berend confronts an underground fire and financial speculators by designing a protective safety apparatus and proving that disciplined scientific ingenuity can triumph over both nature's hazards and human greed.
stories.author: Jókai Mór

stories.title: Pongrácz István gróf különös világa

unit.title: Irony, Satire & Reading Between the Lines

stories.summary: Pongrácz István gróf Nedec várában a középkori lovagkor szabályai szerint él, magánhadsereget tart fenn, és még Beszterce városát is ostrom alá veszi egy vélt sérelem miatt; ám amikor az árva Apolka a várba kerül, a komikus lovagi játék váratlanul mély emberi érzelmekkel telik meg.
stories.author: Mikszáth Kálmán

stories.title: A sólyomröptetés és a távlat fegyelme
stories.summary: A végtelen puszta közepén fekvő elszigetelt sólyomtelepen a fiatal narrátor a madarak idomításának szigorú, hallgatag rendjét figyeli; Lilik, a solymászmester mozdulatai mögött felsejlik a hatalom, a fegyelem és a szabadság rideg, mégis lenyűgöző parabolája.
stories.author: Mészöly Miklós

stories.title: Niki és a kimondhatatlan évek
stories.summary: Az ötvenes évek nyomasztó légkörében Ancsa János mérnököt váratlanul, indoklás nélkül letartóztatják; felesége és a hűséges foxterrier, Niki öt éven át viselik a bürokratikus hallgatás, a társadalmi kiközösítés és a kimondhatatlan szorongás súlyát.
stories.author: Déry Tibor

stories.title: Vihar a kávéházban: Publicisztika és vitairat
stories.summary: In the smoky swirl of the Café Meteor, the fiery poet and essayist Endre Ady refines a blistering political editorial with his cautious editor, defending his uncompromising stance against aristocratic complacency and intellectual lethargy.
stories.author: Ady Endre

stories.title: A szóbeszéd hatalma Rómában
stories.summary: In imperial Rome, the young emperor Nero is tormented by rumors that the populace mocks his verses, while his aging tutor Seneca attempts to teach him the difference between distorted gossip and verified truth.
stories.author: Kosztolányi Dezső

stories.title: Szakhmáry Zoltán tervei és a nagy szavak
stories.summary: On a sprawling Great Plain manor, the visionary yet indebted gentleman farmer Zoltán Szakhmáry passionately unveils his grand modernizing plans to the cynical, hedonistic landowner Csuli Csörgheő, relying on soaring rhetorical frames to mask his impending ruin.
stories.author: Móricz Zsigmond

stories.title: A puszta világa és a horizont
stories.summary: Illyés Gyula megidézi a dunántúli uradalmi puszták zárt világát, ahol a horizont végtelensége és a cselédsors küzdelmei egy sajátos, szívós és méltóságteljes emberi jellemet formáltak meg.
stories.author: Illyés Gyula

stories.title: A föld, a munka és a felemelkedés ára
stories.summary: Veres Péter felidézi a paraszti sors küzdelmeit és az önművelés rögös útját, párbeszédet folytatva a gazdával a tanulás, a földhöz kötöttség és a társadalmi kitörés áldozatairól.
stories.author: Veres Péter

stories.title: Változó világok és a múlt mérlege
stories.summary: A kárpáti kastély csendjében Henrik tábornok és Konrád negyvenegy év után találkozik újra, hogy mérleget vonjanak barátságukról, az eltűnt Monarchia gazdasági és társadalmi rendjéről, valamint a világot felforgató válságokról.
stories.author: Márai Sándor

stories.title: Emerenc és a bizalom határai
stories.summary: Az idős, rejtélyes házvezetőnő, Emerenc és a fiatal írónő kapcsolatának kibontakozása, amelyben a szeretet, a méltóság és a generációk közötti távolság kérdései feszülnek egymásnak.
stories.author: Szabó Magda
topics: Demographics, generations and the life course

stories.title: Hidak, bérházak és budai udvarok
stories.summary: Bébé és Medve Gábor a budai hegyoldal és a Duna-part zegzugos utcáit járva a városi terek rejtett geometriájáról, a bérházak körfolyosóiról és a múló idő kőbe vésett nyomairól beszélgetnek.
stories.author: Ottlik Géza

stories.title: A Kis-Balaton nádasa és Matula bácsi bölcsessége
stories.summary: Tutajos és az öreg pákász, Matula bácsi a Kis-Balaton sűrű nádasában csónakázva a természet belső törvényeiről, a vadvilág tiszteletéről és az emberi beavatkozás határairól beszélgetnek.
stories.author: Fekete István

stories.title: Törvény, igazság és vármegyei hatalom
stories.summary: Tengelyi Jónás tiszaréti jegyző és a törvényen kívülivé lett Viola találkozása a nádas szélén: drámai vita a vármegyei nemesi önkényről, a törvények rideg betűjéről és az igazság valódi természetéről.
stories.author: Eötvös József

stories.title: Szembenézés a történelemmel és az emberi méltóság
stories.summary: Köves Gyuri hazatérése a koncentrációs táborokból a háború utáni budapesti bérházba: megrázó párbeszéd az idős szomszéddal a sorsról, a személyes döntésekről és az emberi méltóság megtartásáról az abszurditásban.
stories.author: Kertész Imre

stories.title: Szülőföld, anyanyelv és megtartó közösség
stories.summary: Sütő András hazalátogatása szülőfalujába, Pusztakamarásra idős édesanyjához: szívszorító és felemelő beszélgetés a mezőségi szülőföldről, az anyanyelv megőrzéséről, a határok feletti összetartozásról és az emberi megmaradásról.
stories.author: Sütő András

stories.title: Anyanyelv és haza az emigrációban
stories.summary: Márai Sándor és felesége, Lola az olaszországi Posillipóban és New Yorkban élik meg az emigráció magányát, ahol az író számára az anyanyelv marad az egyetlen igazi hazája és menedéke.
stories.author: Márai Sándor

stories.title: Politikai egyensúlyozás a vihar előtt
stories.summary: Abády Balázs gróf és a külügyminiszter a bécsi Ballhausplatz szalonjában a fenyegető európai háború árnyékában tárgyalnak a Monarchia szövetségi politikájáról és a szuverenitás megőrzéséről.
stories.author: Bánffy Miklós

stories.title: Buttler János pere az intézményi önkény ellen
stories.summary: Buttler János gróf az egyházi és világi hatóságok cinkosságával ráerőszakolt házasság érvénytelenítéséért küzd, miközben ügyvédjével a jogi eljárás és a hivatali közöny buktatóit mérlegelik.
stories.author: Mikszáth Kálmán
topics: Civic participation, advocacy and public institutions

stories.summary: The history and adoption of Hungary's Fundamental Law on Easter Monday 2011, replacing the amended 1949 constitution.

stories.title: A Nemzeti hitvallás: a nemzet közös értékei
stories.summary: The preamble of the Fundamental Law, the National Avowal, which honors Saint Stephen and affirms national identity.

stories.title: Szabadság és felelősség: az alapvető jogok védelme
stories.summary: The bill of rights in the Fundamental Law, guaranteeing human dignity, personal freedom, and civic equality.

stories.title: Az állami berendezkedés és a közösség érdeke
stories.summary: The organization of the state, the principle of separation of powers, and the civic obligations of citizens.

stories.title: Az Alkotmánybíróság és a sarkalatos törvények garanciája
stories.summary: The role of the Constitutional Court, the Commissioner for Fundamental Rights, and cardinal laws in safeguarding democracy.

stories.title: Az Alaptörvény: Magyarország alkotmányos rendje
stories.summary: A comprehensive overview of Hungary's Fundamental Law: its historical background, the National Avowal, fundamental rights, state structure, and constitutional safeguards.

stories.title: A magyar állampolgárság megszerzése és jogi alapjai
stories.summary: The legal foundation of Hungarian citizenship: the principle of descent (jus sanguinis), naturalization paths, proof of ancestry, and dual citizenship status recognized under Hungarian law.

stories.title: Alapvető jogok: Választójog, szabadságjogok és emberi méltóság
stories.summary: Exploring the fundamental constitutional rights of Hungarian citizens: the right to vote in national and European elections, freedoms of speech and assembly, petition rights, and consular protection abroad.

stories.title: Állampolgári kötelességek: A haza védelme és a közös teherviselés
stories.summary: Understanding constitutional civic duties: paying taxes in proportion to capacity (közteherviselés), national defense obligations, mandatory schooling for children, environmental protection, and obedience to the law.
topics: Civic Duty & Obligation Syntax: Kötelessége [Infinitivus], Tartozik

stories.title: Az állampolgársági eskü és a ceremónia magasztossága
stories.summary: The emotional pinnacle of naturalization: the solemn citizenship oath administered by the mayor, pledging loyalty to Hungary and the Fundamental Law before the national tricolor while singing the Himnusz.

stories.summary: Culminating preparation for the constitutional basics citizenship exam: mastering Hungarian history, institutions, symbols, and culture, and looking forward to an active civic life as a proud Hungarian.

stories.summary: The National Assembly in the Hungarian Parliament building, its 199 representatives, unicameral structure, and legislative powers.

stories.title: A köztársasági elnök: a nemzet egységének őre
stories.summary: The President of the Republic residing in the Sándor Palace, expressing the unity of the nation and guarding democratic balance.

stories.title: A Kormány és a miniszterelnök: a végrehajtó hatalom vezetése
stories.summary: The Government led by the Prime Minister in the Carmelite Monastery, managing the state and directing administration.

stories.title: A bíróságok és az ügyészség: a független igazságszolgáltatás
stories.summary: The administration of justice through independent courts headed by the Curia, and the role of the public prosecution service.

stories.title: A törvényhozás útja és a közvetlen demokrácia
stories.summary: How a bill becomes law, its promulgation in the Magyar Közlöny, and the mechanism of national referendums.

stories.title: A modern magyar államszervezet és demokratikus intézményei
stories.summary: A comprehensive guide to Hungary's contemporary state architecture: the National Assembly, the President of the Republic, the Government, independent courts, and the legislative process.

stories.title: Károly Róbert és a gazdasági rend
stories.summary: Following the extinction of the Árpád dynasty, Charles Robert of Anjou restored central authority in Hungary, broke the power of the oligarchs, and created economic prosperity with Europe's most famous gold florin.

stories.title: A visegrádi királytalálkozó
stories.summary: In 1335, Charles Robert hosted a historic diplomatic congress in the royal palace of Visegrád with the kings of Bohemia and Poland, forging alliances and opening new trade routes.

stories.title: Nagy Lajos és az 1351-es törvények
stories.summary: King Louis the Great, celebrated as a chivalric monarch, expanded Hungary's power across Poland and Italy and enshrined fundamental noble liberties in the 1351 laws.

stories.title: Zsigmond és a déli végvárrendszer
stories.summary: Sigismund of Luxembourg, king of Hungary and Holy Roman Emperor, recognized the rising Ottoman peril and pioneered a formidable double chain of border fortresses.

stories.title: Hunyadi János és a nándorfehérvári diadal
stories.summary: In July 1456, governor János Hunyadi and crusader friar John of Capistrano repelled Mehmed II's siege of Belgrade, securing Hungary and inspiring the worldwide midday church bell decree.

stories.title: Az Anjouk és a középkori királyok
stories.summary: The complete chronological saga of 14th and 15th century Hungary: from Charles Robert's financial revival and the 1335 Visegrád summit to Louis the Great's knightly empire, Sigismund's border fortifications, and Hunyadi's immortal victory at Nándorfehérvár in 1456.

stories.title: Az Árpád-házi királyok
stories.summary: After István, the House of Árpád kept the Hungarian throne for nearly three centuries: I. László the border-defender, Könyves Kálmán the scholar-king, and II. András, whose reign set the stage for the Golden Bull.

stories.title: Az Aranybulla
stories.summary: Why the nobility pressed II. András for a written charter, what the Golden Bull of 1222 actually guaranteed, and why historians compare it to England's Magna Carta.
topics: aki és amely: személyek és dolgok

stories.title: Az ország megszervezése
stories.summary: The county system that governed the kingdom, the catastrophe of the 1241-42 Mongol invasion, and IV. Béla's stone-castle rebuilding programme afterward.
topics: a vonatkozó névmás esetei: akit, akinek, akik

stories.title: Egyház és állam
stories.summary: How the church's dioceses and monasteries were organized alongside the kingdom, the 1083 canonizations, and the church's economic and political role.
topics: ahol és amikor: hely- és időhatározói mellékmondatok

stories.title: Az Árpád-ház vége
stories.summary: The weakening of royal power under the last Árpád kings, III. András's brief reign, and the male line's extinction in 1301.

stories.title: The Árpád Dynasty
stories.summary: A synthesis of the Árpád dynasty's nearly four-century rule after István: notable kings, the Golden Bull of 1222, the kingdom's consolidation through the tatárjárás, church and state, and the male line's extinction in 1301.
topics: aki és amely: személyek és dolgok

stories.title: Az alkotmányos rend és a jogállamiság fundamentuma
stories.location: Budapest, az Alkotmánybíróság Donáti utcai épülete és a Kúria
stories.summary: Modern Hungary is a democratic state governed by the rule of law. The Fundamental Law (Alaptörvény) guarantees fundamental human rights and establishes the separation of powers between legislative, executive, and judicial branches. The Constitutional Court and the independent judiciary ensure that state authority never exceeds its lawful limits, protecting citizens' freedom.

stories.title: A magyar államszervezet és a parlamentáris demokrácia
stories.location: Budapest, Országház, a budavári Sándor-palota és egy Pest vármegyei községháza
stories.summary: Hungary's political system is a parliamentary representative democracy. The 199 Members of the National Assembly are elected every four years. The President of the Republic in the Sándor Palace acts as head of state, symbolizing the nation's unity, while the Prime Minister leads the executive Government, accountable to Parliament. Local municipalities govern towns and villages.

stories.title: A NATO-csatlakozás (1999) és Magyarország biztonsága
stories.summary: Following an overwhelming 85% majority in the November 1997 referendum, Hungary officially joined the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) on March 12, 1999 in Independence, Missouri, alongside Poland and the Czech Republic. Article 5 of the Washington Treaty guaranteed collective defense, integrating Hungary into the democratic transatlantic security community.

stories.title: Csatlakozás az Európai Unióhoz (2004) és a schengeni határok
stories.location: Budapest, Városliget (Időkerék) és a szlovák-magyar határ az Ipoly partján
stories.summary: On May 1, 2004, Hungary fulfilled a historic ambition by officially joining the European Union. At Budapest's City Park, the massive Time Wheel turned to mark the historic hour. Accession brought the four EU freedoms—free movement of goods, services, capital, and persons. In December 2007, joining the Schengen Area physically erased the border barriers separating Hungarians from Austria and Slovakia.

stories.title: A nemzetpolitika és a határon túli magyarság összetartozása
stories.location: Kolozsvár, Szabadka, a Parlament Főrendiházi terme és a Nemzeti Összetartozás Emlékhelye
stories.summary: The 1920 Trianon Treaty severed one-third of ethnic Hungarians into neighboring states. Under the Fundamental Law, the Hungarian state bears constitutional responsibility for cross-border communities in Transylvania, Upper Hungary, Vojvodina, and Transcarpathia. The 2010 simplified naturalization law enabled over one million kin-state Hungarians to regain citizenship, while June 4th was proclaimed the Day of National Cohesion.

stories.title: A modern demokratikus Magyarország és az euroatlanti integráció
stories.location: Budapest, Országház, Sándor-palota és a Kárpát-medence
stories.summary: A comprehensive panoramic chronicle of modern democratic Hungary. From the constitutional framework of the rule of law, the separation of powers, and the Fundamental Law; the institutional workings of the National Assembly, the President of the Republic, and local self-governments; the historic security guarantee of NATO accession in 1999; EU membership in 2004 and the Schengen borderless zone in 2007; to modern kin-state policy supporting cross-border Hungarians through dual citizenship and national cohesion.

stories.title: A fejedelemség megszületése
stories.summary: Following Buda's fall in 1541, Queen Isabella and her infant son John Sigismund established the autonomous Principality of Transylvania in Gyulafehérvár, paying tribute to the sultan while maintaining internal Hungarian statehood.

stories.title: A tordai vallásbéke (1568)
stories.summary: At the 1568 Diet of Torda, Transylvania enacted Europe's first law on universal religious tolerance, granting equal legal protection to Catholic, Lutheran, Reformed, and Unitarian believers amid bloody religious wars across the continent.

stories.title: Bethlen Gábor és a gazdasági felvirágzás
stories.summary: Prince Gábor Bethlen (1613–1629) ushered in Transylvania's Golden Age through state monopolies on salt and mining, attracting skilled foreign craftsmen and founding the illustrious princely academy in Gyulafehérvár.

stories.title: Erdély a harmincéves háborúban
stories.summary: During the Thirty Years' War, Bethlen Gábor allied with Protestant European powers against the Habsburg Emperor, capturing Upper Hungary and securing constitutional freedoms in the 1621 Peace of Nikolsburg.

stories.title: A magyar nyelv és kultúra menedéke
stories.summary: While the central plains suffered Ottoman devastation, Transylvania flourished as the sanctuary of Hungarian literature, vernacular education, and psalm translation, cementing the enduring foundation of modern national consciousness.

stories.title: Erdély aranykora és történelmi öröksége
stories.summary: The glorious golden age of the Principality of Transylvania: its establishment after Buda's fall in 1541, the revolutionary 1568 Diet of Torda proclaiming universal religious freedom, Prince Gábor Bethlen's mercantilist economic boom and academic patronage, participation in the Thirty Years' War, and its enduring role as the cultural sanctuary of the Hungarian language.

stories.title: Eső és forradalom Pesten
stories.summary: March 15, 1848 begins on a cold, pouring morning in Pest. Petőfi and the March Youth gather at the Pilvax coffee house, marching through wet cobblestone streets to Landerer's printing press to seize freedom of the press without shedding a drop of blood.

stories.title: Mit kíván a magyar nemzet?
stories.summary: On the afternoon of March 15, thousands gather outside the National Museum in the rain. Vasvári and Jókai read out the Twelve Points: an independent ministry, emancipation of the serfs, equality before the law, and the release of political prisoner Táncsics.

stories.title: A törvényes forradalom és a függetlenség
stories.summary: Batthyány forms Hungary's first responsible government, and the April Laws transform the kingdom into a modern civic state. But when the Habsburg court attacks, the parliament retreats to Debrecen, where Kossuth proclaims full independence in the Great Church.

stories.title: A tavaszi hadjárat csodája
stories.summary: The young Honvéd army, led by the brilliant Artúr Görgei, performs miracles during the Spring Campaign of 1849. At Hatvan, Tápióbicske, and Isaszeg, the Hungarian forces smash the imperial armies and retake Buda, terrifying Vienna.

stories.title: Világos és az aradi vértanúk öröksége
stories.summary: Faced with overwhelming Austrian and Russian forces, Görgei lays down arms at Világos before the Russian general. The brutal Austrian retribution executes Batthyány and the Thirteen Martyrs at Arad, turning their sacrifice into the eternal cornerstone of Hungarian liberty.

stories.title: Az 1848–49-es forradalom és szabadságharc
stories.summary: The epic story of 1848–49: from the rainy morning at Pilvax and the Twelve Points, through the April Laws and Kossuth's proclamation in Debrecen, to the glorious Spring Campaign and the tragic sacrifice of the Arad Martyrs.

stories.title: A Királyi Magyarország és Pozsony
stories.summary: Following Mohács and the fall of Buda, the northern and western parts of Hungary came under Habsburg rule as Royal Hungary, with Pozsony (Bratislava) serving as the kingdom's coronation capital and administrative center.

stories.title: Buda 1541-es elfoglalása és a Hódoltság
stories.summary: On August 29, 1541, Sultan Suleiman captured Buda Castle through trickery without firing a shot, establishing the Ottoman-ruled territory (Hódoltság) across the heart of Hungary for 150 years.

stories.title: Erdély: A magyar kultúra és a vallásszabadság bástyája
stories.summary: In the east, the Principality of Transylvania arose under John Sigismund and later princes. Headquartered in Gyulafehérvár, Transylvania preserved Hungarian language and enacted Europe's first law on religious tolerance in 1568.

stories.title: Végvári élet és mezővárosi virágzás a határokon
stories.summary: Along the border fortress chain (Eger, Szigetvár, Győr), heroic border warriors fought daily skirmishes. Concurrently, the agricultural market towns of the Great Plain grew wealthy trading Hungarian grey cattle to western Europe.

stories.title: Másfél évszázad megosztottságban
stories.summary: Between 1541 and 1699, Hungary endured 150 years of tripartite division. Despite widespread destruction, the legal unity of the Hungarian crown, culture, and language endured until Buda's liberation in 1686.

stories.title: A három részre szakadt Magyarország (1541–1699)
stories.summary: The dramatic 150-year era of the tripartite partition of Hungary (1541–1699): Royal Hungary under Habsburg rule with Pozsony as capital, the Ottoman Hódoltság centered in Buda, the autonomous Principality of Transylvania championing religious freedom, heroic border fortress defense, cattle trade, and the eventual liberation of Buda in 1686.

stories.title: Miért indultak nyugatra a magyar törzsek
stories.summary: Why, after centuries on the Pontic steppe, mounting pressure from the Pechenegs forced the Magyar tribal confederation to abandon Etelköz and set out west toward the Carpathians.
topics: Miért indultak nyugatra a magyar törzsek

stories.title: Átkelés a Kárpátokon
stories.summary: How the Magyar tribes crossed the Carpathian mountains around 895, traditionally through the Verecke Pass, and what let their light cavalry and archers move so effectively.

stories.title: Árpád és a hét törzs
stories.summary: How the seven Magyar tribes, according to tradition, united under a blood oath and were led into the new homeland by Árpád, founder of the ruling Árpád dynasty.
topics: nevesített alanyok: Árpád és a hét törzs

stories.title: A medence birtokba vétele
stories.summary: How the Magyar tribes gradually occupied the Carpathian Basin over several years, absorbing or displacing the peoples already there, and secured their new home at the Battle of Pozsony in 907.

stories.title: A honfoglalás a nemzeti emlékezetben
stories.summary: Why 895 and the honfoglalás remain central to Hungarian national identity today, from the turul bird and the Csodaszarvas legend to the Millennium Monument — and why it matters for the citizenship exam.

stories.location: Budapest, Országház és a Gellért Szálló
stories.summary: Following the collapse of 1918 and the turmoil of the Soviet Republic, Hungary restored its constitutional form as a kingdom. On March 1, 1920, the National Assembly elected former Austro-Hungarian admiral Miklós Horthy as Regent (kormányzó), establishing a unique political system: a kingdom without a king.

stories.title: A bethleni konszolidáció és a pengő sikere
stories.location: Budapest, Sándor-palota és a Magyar Nemzeti Bank
stories.summary: Count István Bethlen assumed the prime ministership in 1921, launching an extraordinary decade of political and financial stabilization. Through a major League of Nations loan, he established the National Bank and introduced the pengő, rescuing the nation from runaway inflation.

stories.title: Klebelsberg Kuno és a kultúrfölény programja
stories.location: Szeged, Dóm tér és egy alföldi tanyasi népiskola
stories.summary: Count Kuno Klebelsberg, minister of education, launched a legendary cultural renaissance. Believing that Hungary could regain its international respect through knowledge and intellectual excellence ('kultúrfölény'), he built 5,000 rural elementary schools, relocated universities to Szeged and Debrecen, and established Collegium Hungaricum institutes across Europe.

stories.title: A két háború közötti társadalom: Fények és árnyak
characters: Budapesti újságíró a New York kávéházban
stories.location: Budapest, New York Kávéház és a dél-alföldi falu
stories.summary: Hungarian society between the wars was a study in contrasts. While Budapest flourished with world-class coffeehouses, cinema, and literary magazines like 'Nyugat', the rural countryside was burdened by rigid landed estates and millions of struggling agrarian laborers.

stories.title: A revíziós sikerek és az első bécsi döntés (1938)
stories.location: Bécs, Belvedere kastély és Kassa főtere
stories.summary: Hungary pursued peaceful territorial revision throughout the interwar years. Following the Munich conference, the First Vienna Award on November 2, 1938, returned predominantly ethnic Hungarian areas of southern Slovakia (Felvidék) to Hungary, triggering national euphoria but deepening diplomatic dependence on the Axis powers.

stories.title: A Horthy-korszak története: Konszolidáció, kultúra és revízió (1920–1939)
characters: Gróf Bethlen István és Gróf Klebelsberg Kuno
stories.location: Budapest, Szeged, Kassa és az Alföld
stories.summary: A complete historical synthesis of interwar Hungary: the election of Regent Miklós Horthy in 1920, Count Bethlen's monetary and political consolidation with the pengő, Count Klebelsberg's cultural and educational breakthrough (Szent-Györgyi's Nobel Prize), social realities of 'úri Magyarország', and the diplomatic revisionism leading to the First Vienna Award in 1938.

stories.title: A kádári kiegyezés: a megtorlástól a konszolidációig
stories.location: Budapest, a Parlament és a Margit körúti börtön kapuja
stories.summary: After the brutal bloodbath and executions of 1956-1961, János Kádár realized terror alone could not stabilize his rule. In 1961 he reversed Rákosi's totalitarian formula, declaring 'whoever is not against us is with us'. With the 1963 general amnesty, a quiet, cynical compromise was forged: political acquiescence in exchange for private peace and material security.

stories.title: Az Új Gazdasági Mechanizmus (1968)
stories.location: Budapest, Tervhivatal és egy alföldi termelőszövetkezet
stories.summary: On January 1, 1968, Hungary launched the New Economic Mechanism under reform economist Rezső Nyers. Departing from rigid Soviet central planning, it introduced enterprise autonomy, profit incentives, and legal room for household farming ('háztáji'). The second economy allowed millions to augment their income through diligent private work.

stories.title: A legvidámabb barakk és a gulyáskommunizmus
stories.location: Siófok és a budapesti Skála áruház
stories.summary: In the 1970s, Western observers dubbed Hungary 'the happiest barrack' of the Soviet bloc. 'Goulash communism' (or 'refrigerator socialism') promised meat on the table, affordable consumer goods, small weekend garden plots, and summer holidays at Lake Balaton. While people waited years for a Trabant car, life seemed remarkably comfortable compared to Romania or the USSR.

stories.title: A három T világa: kultúrpolitika és szamizdat
stories.location: Budapest, a Szépirodalmi Könyvkiadó és egy zuglói pince
stories.summary: Kádár's cultural supremo, György Aczél, managed artistic life through the legendary 'Three Ts': támogatott (supported), tűrt (tolerated), and tiltott (prohibited). While regime-friendly art received funding and critical literature was gingerly tolerated, true dissidents were banned. By the late 1970s, underground intellectuals established samizdat networks and published the illegal journal Beszélő.

stories.title: Adósságcsapda és a rendszer kifulladása (1980-as évek)
stories.location: Budapest, Magyar Nemzeti Bank és az Építők Rózsa Ferenc Művelődési Háza
stories.summary: The illusion of socialist prosperity was financed not by superior productivity, but by skyrocketing Western loans. The global oil crises and structural inefficiencies plunged Hungary into an inescapable debt spiral. In 1982 Hungary joined the IMF to avert immediate default. By 1988, as living standards fell, an exhausted János Kádár was removed, paving the path toward systemic collapse.

stories.title: A Kádár-korszak története: a gulyáskommunizmustól a válságig (1956–1988)
stories.location: Budapest, a Parlament, a Balaton és az Építők Művelődési Háza
stories.summary: A panoramic historical chronicle of the Kádár era spanning 1956 to 1988. From the brutal post-1956 retributions to the 1963 amnesty and the pragmatism of 'whoever is not against us is with us'; the economic experiment of the 1968 New Economic Mechanism and second economy; the consumer illusion of 'goulash communism' and 'the happiest barrack'; cultural governance through the 'Three Ts' and the rise of samizdat dissidents; ending with the debt crisis of the 1980s that brought the socialist model to systemic exhaustion.

stories.title: A csendes dac és a passzív ellenállás
stories.summary: Following the tragic defeat of 1849, the Austrian minister Alexander Bach installs a suffocating police bureaucracy. But Hungarians invent passive resistance: refusing to speak German, ignoring imperial decrees, and practicing stubborn tax refusal while wearing traditional Hungarian coats.

stories.title: A Haza Bölcse és a Húsvéti cikk
stories.summary: Ferenc Deák, residing in the modest Queen of England Hotel in Pest, carves wooden boxes, smokes his pipe, and bides his time. On Easter 1865, he pens the legendary Easter Article in Pesti Napló, offering a brilliant, realistic compromise based on the 1723 Pragmatic Sanction.

stories.title: A koronázás fényei és Erzsébet királyné
stories.summary: On June 8, 1867, Budapest witnesses one of the most dazzling spectacles in European history. In the Matthias Church, Franz Joseph is crowned with Saint Stephen's Crown, while the beloved Queen Elisabeth ('Sisi'), wearing a dress by Charles Worth, seals the reconciliation.

stories.title: A dualizmus világa: Közös ügyek és önállóság
stories.summary: The Austro-Hungarian Monarchy is established as a unique dual-state superpower. Emperor Franz Joseph reigns over both halves, foreign affairs and the army are managed jointly, but in Pest, a sovereign parliament and prime minister govern Hungarian domestic destiny.

stories.title: A gazdasági robbanás és a jogfolytonosság
stories.summary: With peace secured, Hungary experiences an unprecedented economic explosion. Capital pours into railways, banks, and factories; Buda and Pest unite into Budapest in 1873. The historical legacy of 1867 preserved the continuity of Hungarian constitutional law.

stories.title: A kiegyezés és a dualizmus születése
stories.summary: From the stubborn passive resistance of the Bach era and Deák's masterly Easter Article, to the glittering coronation of Franz Joseph and Sisi in 1867, and the golden decades of economic growth that transformed Budapest into a world metropolis.

stories.summary: How the devastated plains of Hungary were repopulated after the Ottoman wars by German Swabians, Slovaks, and Serbs, creating a colorful multinational state.

stories.summary: The dramatic moment in Pozsony when the Hungarian nobility drew their swords for Maria Theresa with the famous cry: 'Vitam et sanguinem!'

stories.title: Felvilágosult reformok: Urbárium és Ratio Educationis
stories.summary: Maria Theresa's enlightened decrees: the Urbarium limiting feudal peasant labor, and the Ratio Educationis establishing modern primary education.

stories.title: II. József, a kalapos király és rendeletei
stories.summary: Joseph II's controversial rule by decree: the progressive Edict of Tolerance, the resented German language decree, and his deathbed revocations.

stories.title: Nemzeti ébredés és a magyar nyelv mozgalma
stories.summary: How noble resistance to Germanization sparked the mother-tongue revival, György Bessenyei's writings, and the birth of modern Hungarian national identity.

stories.title: A 18. század: újjáépítés és felvilágosodás
stories.summary: The comprehensive saga of 18th-century Hungary: repopulation, Maria Theresa's enlightened absolutism, Joseph II's decrees, and the dawn of national awakening.

stories.title: A hadba lépés tragédiája: Kassa bombázása (1941)
stories.location: Kassa főutcája és a budapesti Országház
stories.summary: On June 26, 1941, unidentified aircraft bombed the city of Kassa. Within hours, Prime Minister László Bárdossy announced in Parliament that a state of war existed between Hungary and the Soviet Union, dragging the nation into the catastrophic vortex of World War II against Teleki Pál's desperate warnings.

stories.title: A doni katasztrófa: Dermesztő pokol a Don-kanyarnál (1943)
stories.location: A Don-kanyar hófúvásai és egy alföldi falu
stories.summary: In January 1943, the Soviet Red Army launched a massive winter offensive at the Don bend. The 200,000-strong 2nd Hungarian Army, strung out along a 200-kilometer front without adequate winter clothing or heavy anti-tank weapons, was obliterated in minus 35-degree cold.

stories.title: A német megszállás és az embermentők helytállása (1944)
stories.location: Budapest, Svéd Nagykövetség és a nemzetközi gettó
stories.summary: On March 19, 1944, Hitler launched Operation Margarethe, occupying Hungary. Under the direction of Adolf Eichmann, over 430,000 rural Hungarian Jews were deported to Auschwitz within weeks. Amidst this dark abyss, brave rescuers like Raoul Wallenberg, Carl Lutz, and Sára Salkaházi risked their lives to save tens of thousands.

stories.title: A kiugrási kísérlet és a nyilas rémuralom (1944. október)
stories.location: Budapest, Magyar Rádió (Bródy Sándor utca) és a Duna-part
stories.summary: On October 15, 1944, Regent Miklós Horthy broadcast a dramatic radio proclamation announcing an armistice with the Soviet Union. However, the German SS kidnapped his son, backed an Arrow Cross fascist coup led by Ferenc Szálasi, and unleashed a reign of terror culminating in Danube bank massacres.

stories.title: Budapest ostroma és a háború vége (1944–1945)
characters: Visszatérő budapesti lakos a romok között
stories.location: A Gellért-hegy barlangjai, Lánchíd romjai és a Várnegyed
stories.summary: The Siege of Budapest was one of the deadliest urban battles of WWII, lasting 102 days. The city was pulverized, all historic Danube bridges were blown up by retreating German forces, and hundreds of thousands hid in basements. Liberation from fascism was immediately followed by Soviet occupation and deportations to forced labor camps.

stories.title: Magyarország a második világháborúban: Hadba lépés, holokauszt és ostrom (1941–1945)

stories.summary: A comprehensive Rest is History narrative synthesizing Hungary's tragedy in World War II: entry into the war following the bombing of Kassa, the catastrophic freezing defeat of the 2nd Army at the Don, German military occupation (March 1944) and the Holocaust, the failed October armistice attempt followed by Arrow Cross terror, and the apocalyptic 102-day Siege of Budapest.

stories.title: Mátyás megválasztása a Duna jegén
stories.summary: In January 1458, the Hungarian nobility gathered on the frozen Danube beneath Buda Castle to elect the young Matthias Corvinus, son of hero János Hunyadi, to the throne.

stories.title: A fekete sereg és a hadviselés
stories.summary: King Matthias established the legendary Black Army, one of Europe's first permanent professional standing armies, securing borders against Ottoman raids and conquering Vienna.

stories.title: A reneszánsz udvar és a Corvina
stories.summary: Under Matthias and Queen Beatrice of Aragon, the royal courts at Buda and Visegrád became Europe's foremost Renaissance centers north of the Alps, home to the famous Corvina library.

stories.title: Mátyás király és az igazságos bíráskodás
stories.summary: Known as 'Matthias the Just', the king modernized taxation through the chimney tax (füstpénz) and entered national folklore as the disguised monarch defending the common folk.

stories.title: Meghalt Mátyás, oda az igazság
stories.summary: When King Matthias died in Vienna in 1490 without a legitimate heir, Hungary entered rapid political fragmentation, crystallizing the enduring proverb 'King Matthias is dead, justice has perished.'

stories.title: Mátyás király és a reneszánsz udvar
stories.summary: The grand historical arc of Renaissance Hungary under King Matthias Corvinus (1458–1490): his dramatic Danube election, the invincible Black Army, European Renaissance patronage and the Corvina library, the legend of 'Matthias the Just', and the national grief following his sudden death in 1490.

stories.title: A meggyengült királyság és a belső viszályok
stories.summary: Following King Matthias's death in 1490, royal central power collapsed under the Jagiellon kings. The brutal suppression of the 1514 Dózsa peasant revolt left Hungarian society deeply divided on the eve of the Ottoman invasion.

stories.title: Szulejmán szultán és Nándorfehérvár eleste
stories.summary: In 1520, the ambitious young Sultan Suleiman the Magnificent came to power in Istanbul. In 1521, the key southern stronghold Nándorfehérvár fell, leaving the Hungarian heartland completely exposed.

stories.title: A tragikus ütközet 1526. augusztus 29-én
stories.summary: On August 29, 1526, on the plains south of Mohács, King Louis II's 25,000 soldiers confronted Sultan Suleiman's 60,000-strong army. Despite a valiant cavalry assault, the Hungarian lines were pulverized by Ottoman cannons within two hours.

stories.title: II. Lajos tragédiája a Csele-patakban
stories.summary: While escaping the battlefield in the stormy dusk, the twenty-year-old King Louis II drowned in the flooded Csele brook when his armored horse stumbled, extinguishing the royal line and throwing Hungary into civil strife.

stories.title: Több is veszett Mohácsnál: A nemzeti emlékezet
stories.summary: The disaster at Mohács in 1526 ended medieval Hungarian great-power status and led to the 150-year Ottoman occupation. It permanently entered national consciousness as the supreme benchmark of tragedy and resilience.

stories.title: A mohácsi csata és a középkori Magyarország bukása
stories.summary: The catastrophic collapse of medieval Hungary at the Battle of Mohács (August 29, 1526): internal disunity after 1514, the rise of Suleiman I and fall of Nándorfehérvár, the two-hour collapse against Ottoman artillery, the drowning of King Louis II in the Csele brook, and the enduring cultural memory encapsulated in 'Több is veszett Mohácsnál'.

stories.title: A kétfejű sas és a Szent Korona
stories.summary: In Rest is History style, we explore the extraordinary bureaucratic and military machinery of the Austro-Hungarian Empire: two sovereign states under one emperor-king, three joint ministries, and a sprawling multinational army speaking a dozen languages.

stories.title: 1896: A birodalom csúcsán – A Millennium
characters: Ybl Miklós és Steindl Imre építészek
stories.summary: Budapest throws the party of the century in 1896 to celebrate the 1000th anniversary of the Hungarian Conquest. From the monumental Heroes' Square to Europe's first underground railway, the kingdom demonstrates its pride and dizzying progress to the world.

stories.title: A kávéházak és paloták városa
stories.location: Budapest, New York Kávéház, Nagykörút, Duna-part
stories.summary: How Pest, Buda and Óbuda merged to become one of the fastest-growing world metropolises. The construction of the Parliament, the sweep of the Grand Boulevard, and the rich coffeehouse culture where literature, journalism and romance flourished.

stories.title: A gőzmalmok és vasutak országa
stories.summary: Behind the glamorous coffeehouses lay industrial might: Budapest was the flour milling capital of the globe, Ganz engineering powered locomotives and European power grids, and an immense railway boom transformed the Hungarian plains into a breadbasket.

stories.title: A boldog békeidők alkonya
stories.summary: As the turn of the century arrived, the golden age of the Belle Époque began to reveal profound tensions. Rural poverty drove hundreds of thousands to emigrate to America, ethnic minorities demanded autonomy, and Europe's old order drifted toward the catastrophe of 1914.

stories.title: Az Osztrák–Magyar Monarchia kora (1867–1914)
characters: Andrássy Gyula és Tisza Kálmán miniszterelnökök
Mechwart András és Steindl Imre alkotók
stories.summary: A comprehensive Rest is History narrative tracing the dual monarchy from the power-sharing compromise to the 1896 Millennium mega-celebration, Budapest's golden age of coffeehouses and heavy industry, and the poignant sunset of the Belle Époque.

stories.title: A magyar tudomány csillagai és a Nobel-díjasok
stories.summary: The remarkable contributions of Hungarian scientists and Nobel laureates to universal human knowledge, from Albert Szent-Györgyi's isolation of Vitamin C in Szeged to Katalin Karikó and Ferenc Krausz's 2023 Nobel prizes.

stories.title: A magyar találmányok és újítók világa
stories.summary: Exploring legendary Hungarian inventions that shaped modern everyday life: Ányos Jedlik's dynamo, Ignác Semmelweis's antiseptic hygiene, László Bíró's ballpoint pen, and Ernő Rubik's world-famous cube.

stories.summary: The monumental legacy of Hungarian music: Ferenc Liszt's piano romanticism, the ethnomusicological revolution of Béla Bartók and Zoltán Kodály, and the global popularity of Hungarian operetta.

stories.summary: A tribute to Hungary's literary and artistic pantheon: the national poetry of Petőfi, Arany, Ady, and József Attila, alongside the visionary canvases of Mihály Munkácsy and Tivadar Csontváry Kosztka.

stories.title: Hungarikumok, népi hagyományok és a világörökség
stories.summary: Exploring distinctive national treasures: official Hungarikums like Tokaji wine and Herend porcelain, folk traditions such as Matyó embroidery and the Mohács Busójárás, and UNESCO World Heritage landscapes.

stories.summary: A comprehensive compendium on Hungary's scientific, musical, literary, and folkloric heritage. From Nobel laureates and revolutionary inventions to classical masterpieces, UNESCO sites, and cherished Hungarikums.
topics: Designation with the Essive-Modal Case: -ként and -ként tartják számon

stories.title: A magyar trikolór és nemzeti színeink története
characters: Zászlóért felelős történész a Nemzeti Múzeumban
stories.summary: Hungary's national flag is a horizontal tricolor of red, white, and green. Established during the Reform Era and codified by the 1848 revolutionary laws, its colors represent strength (red), fidelity (white), and hope (green). From the 1848 cockades to the flag with a cut-out hole in 1956, the tricolor symbolizes the nation's struggle for freedom and sovereignty.

stories.title: A Szent Korona és a koronázási jelvények misztériuma
stories.summary: The Holy Crown of Hungary is Europe's oldest surviving coronation crown. Comprising the Greek Crown (corona graeca) and the Latin Crown (corona latina), crowned with its famous tilted cross, it is not merely an ornament but the legal embodiment of Hungarian statehood through the historic Doctrine of the Holy Crown. Guarded in the Parliament with the scepter, orb, and mantle, it returned home from the US in 1978.

stories.title: Magyarország címere: a kettős kereszt és az Árpád-sávok
stories.location: Budapest, a Magyar Országos Levéltár várbeli kutatóterme
stories.summary: The Coat of Arms of Hungary is an elegant vertically split shield crowned by the Holy Crown. The right field displays the silver apostolic patriarchal cross rising from a golden coronet atop three green hills (Tátra, Mátra, Fátra). The left field features the four silver and four red stripes of the founding Árpád Dynasty, representing Hungary's rivers (Duna, Tisza, Dráva, Száva).

stories.title: A Nemzeti Himnusz: Kölcsey imája és Erkel muzsikája
characters: Szavaló diák a Szatmárcsekei emlékház udvarán
stories.location: Szatmárcseke és a Nemzeti Színház Budapesten
stories.summary: Hungary's National Anthem, 'Isten, áldd meg a magyart', is unique among world anthems: not a martial boast of military conquest, but a profound national prayer. Penned by poet Ferenc Kölcsey on January 22, 1823 in Szatmárcseke and set to immortal music by composer Ferenc Erkel in 1844, it surveys centuries of trials and blessings, asking God's protection for a people who have already suffered for past and future sins.

stories.title: A Szózat: Vörösmarty hűségfogadalma a hazához
stories.location: Székesfehérvár, a budapesti Nemzeti Színház és az Országház lépcsője
stories.summary: Regarded as Hungary's second national anthem, the Szózat ('The Appeal') was written by romantic poet Mihály Vörösmarty in 1836 and set to stirring music by Béni Egressy in 1843. Opening with the immortal imperative 'To your homeland be unwaveringly faithful', it proclaims that the soil of the motherland is the cradle and grave of every Hungarian, concluding ceremonies with an unbreakable pledge of fidelity.

stories.title: Magyarország nemzeti jelképeinek története
stories.location: Budapest, Országház és a Nemzeti Múzeum
stories.summary: A comprehensive panoramic chronicle of Hungary's sacred national symbols enshrined in the Fundamental Law. From the red-white-green tricolor representing strength, fidelity, and hope; the historic Holy Crown and coronation regalia embodying millennial statehood; the crowned coat of arms uniting the apostolic double cross and the Árpád stripes; Kölcsey's Himnusz as the collective national prayer; to Vörösmarty's Szózat as the steadfast pledge of fidelity to the motherland.

stories.title: Kossuth Lajos Amerikában és a világban
stories.summary: After the defeat of 1849, Kossuth escapes to the Ottoman Empire and embarks on a historic tour across Great Britain and America. Speaking in rich, Shakespearean English, his oratorical brilliance enchants hundreds of thousands, turning him into a global champion of liberty.

stories.title: Petőfi Sándor, a lánglelkű költő
stories.summary: Petőfi Sándor lived like a comet: passionate, uncompromising, and dedicated to the people. He wrote masterpieces on rickety tavern tables and insisted on riding to the frontline in Transylvania under General Bem, meeting a mysterious heroic death at Segesvár.

stories.title: A Nemzeti dal születése és hatalma
stories.summary: How Petőfi wrote the immortal 'Nemzeti dal' just days before March 15. The thunderous opening line 'Talpra magyar, hí a haza!' and the collective oath 'Esküszünk, esküszünk!' became the battle-cry of a whole nation that echoes across Hungarian history.

stories.title: Kokárda a szívek felett: Nemzeti jelképeink
stories.summary: The origins of Hungary's beloved national symbols: how Szendrey Júlia sewed the first tricolor cockade for Petőfi, the deep meaning of the red-white-green colors, and the debate between the Holy Crown and the republican Kossuth coat of arms.

stories.title: Március 15.: Miért ünnepel a nemzet?
stories.summary: March 15 is one of Hungary's three official national holidays and a central topic on the citizenship interview. Across cities and diaspora communities, citizens pin cockades, lay wreaths at Petőfi statues, and celebrate the birth of modern civic Hungary.

stories.title: Kossuth, Petőfi és a nemzeti szimbólumok
stories.summary: The heroes and symbols of 1848: Kossuth's global crusade in exile, Petőfi's blazing poetry and sacrifice at Segesvár, the electric vow of the Nemzeti dal, the tricolor cockade, and the lasting meaning of March 15 in modern Hungarian civic life.

stories.title: Március 15.: A szabadság és a polgári Magyarország születése
characters: Kokárdás diák a Nemzeti Múzeum lépcsőjén
stories.location: Budapest, Pilvax kávéház és a Nemzeti Múzeum kertje
stories.summary: March 15th is Hungary's most joyous and inspiring national holiday, commemorating the 1848 Revolution. From the gathering of Petőfi and Jókai at the Pilvax Café to the printing of the 12 Points and the National Song at Landerer's press without censorship, and the sea of umbrellas outside the National Museum, March 15th marks the birth of modern civic Hungary.

stories.title: Augusztus 20.: Szent István napja és az államalapítás ünnepe
characters: Frissen felavatott honvédtiszt a Kossuth téren
Családanya a Duna-parton az esti tűzijátéknál
stories.location: Budapest, Kossuth tér, a Szent István-bazilika és a Duna-part
stories.summary: August 20th is Hungary's oldest national holiday and the official state holiday. Commemorating the 1083 canonization of King Saint Stephen and the founding of the Christian Hungarian state in the year 1000, it is celebrated with the raising of the flag and officer inauguration on Kossuth Square, the blessing of the new bread, the Saint Right procession, and evening fireworks over the Danube.

stories.title: Október 23.: A szabadságharc és a köztársaság kettős ünnepe
stories.location: Budapest, Bem tér, Corvin köz és a Parlament Kossuth tere
stories.summary: October 23rd carries double historic weight: it marks the outbreak of the heroic 1956 Revolution against Soviet tyranny and, on its 33rd anniversary in 1989, the official proclamation of the free and democratic Republic of Hungary. From the university students at the Bem statue in 1956 to the jubilant crowds at Kossuth Square in 1989, October 23rd embodies Hungary's unquenchable thirst for freedom.

stories.title: Nemzeti emléknapok: Aradi vértanúk és az Összetartozás Napja
characters: Erdélyi magyar diák a Nemzeti Összetartozás Emlékhelyénél
stories.location: Arad, a vesztőhely és a budapesti Alkotmány utca
stories.summary: Alongside the three national holidays, Hungary observes official national days of remembrance. October 6th is the National Day of Mourning for the 13 martyred generals executed in Arad and Prime Minister Count Lajos Batthyány executed in Pest in 1849. June 4th is the Day of National Cohesion, transforming the trauma of the 1920 Trianon Treaty into a celebration of cross-border unity and cultural survival.

stories.title: A diktatúrák áldozatai: Február 25. és Április 16.
stories.location: Budapest, Terror Háza Múzeum (Andrássy út 60.) és a Duna-part
stories.summary: Hungary honors the victims of 20th-century totalitarianism on two solemn remembrance days. February 25th marks the Memorial Day for Victims of Communist Dictatorships, commemorating the 1947 illegal arrest of MP Béla Kovács and the suffering of hundreds of thousands in Recsk, Gulag camps, and show trials. April 16th is the Holocaust Memorial Day, marking the 1944 ghettoization of Hungarian Jewry.

stories.title: Magyarország nemzeti ünnepei és emléknapjai
stories.location: Budapest, Kossuth tér, Hősök tere és a Nemzeti Múzeum
stories.summary: A comprehensive panoramic chronicle of Hungary's three official national holidays and solemn remembrance days. From March 15th (1848 Civic Revolution, cockades, 12 Points); August 20th (King Saint Stephen, State Founding, New Bread); October 23rd (1956 Revolution and 1989 Republic); October 6th (Martyrs of Arad); June 4th (Day of National Cohesion); to February 25th and April 16th (Victims of Communism and the Holocaust). These days define Hungarian historical consciousness, identity, and civic duty.

stories.summary: The constitutional foundations of Hungarian local government: municipal autonomy, villages, towns, and capital districts.

stories.summary: The executive leadership of the mayor, legislative function of the representative body, and administrative role of the town clerk.

stories.summary: Hungary's 19 counties, Saint Stephen's historical royal counties, the county assembly, and cities with county rights.

stories.title: A kormányablakok és a járási hivatalok világa
stories.summary: State territorial administration, county government offices headed by the főispán, districts, and the one-stop Citizen Windows.

stories.title: Helyi közszolgáltatások és a helyi demokrácia eszközei
stories.summary: Municipal public services (utilities, kindergartens, waste management), municipal taxes, public hearings, and local referendums.

stories.title: Helyi önkormányzatok és területi közigazgatás Magyarországon
stories.summary: A comprehensive compendium on local self-government, municipalities, mayors, counties, Citizen Windows, and public services in Hungary.

stories.title: Hol van Magyarország?
stories.summary: Where Hungary lies in Central Europe, how the Carpathian Basin shapes its geography, and why the Hungarian language is a unique Finno-Ugric island among its neighbours.

stories.title: Megyék, folyók és városok
stories.summary: Hungary's major geographic landscapes, the Danube and Tisza river systems, Lake Balaton, the nineteen counties, and key regional cities beyond Budapest.

stories.title: A zászló és a címer
stories.summary: The deep symbolism of the Hungarian red-white-green flag, the Árpád stripes and apostolic double cross on the coat of arms, and the historical veneration of the Holy Crown.

stories.title: Magyarország szomszédai
stories.summary: Hungary's seven neighbouring states, the geopolitical landscape, the Schengen borders, and the historical Hungarian communities living across the borders.

stories.title: Első áttekintés: A honosítási beszélgetés
stories.summary: An authentic simulation of the naturalization interview where the applicant confidently presents Hungary's geography, national symbols, and borders.
